newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares rise in brisk trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares rise in brisk trade.

text.p: Egyptian share prices ended up on Tuesday in active trade, heavily dominated by the popular housing firm Heliopolis, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index closed 1.21 points higher at 285.93 on a healthy volume of 81.05 million pounds ($23.84 million).
"This is an opportunity for buying," Adel el-Dakroury of Triple A Securities told Reuters. "The big local players seek to sell in December to end the year with a lot of cash and profits."
Heliopolis Housing and Development got the lion's share of trade with shares worth 31.69 million pounds changing hands. It closed unchanged at 430.
"The housing sector is the bourse's 'Black Horse' and Heliopolis, on top of it, is still in demand," Dakroury said.

Paints and Chemical Industries/PACHIN, which has distributed a 6.5 pound dividend per share for 1995/96, was second on the top ten list in terms of turnover, with 6.98 million pounds traded. The share ended 7.00 pounds up at 127.00.
"It still has a long way to go," Dakroury said.
The milling sector was affected by the pre-holidays profit-taking and closed mixed.
East Delta Flour Mills closed 0.25 up at 52.45, but Upper Egypt Flour Mills closed 1.51 lower at 60.99 and Central and West Delta Flour Mills fell 2.00 to 79.15.
The CMAindex for openly traded firms rose to 429.28 from 427.40 on Monday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms also went up to 201.29 from 200.45.
Of the 74 shares traded, 28 rose, 23 fell and 23 ended the day unchanged, the CMA said.
